newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed, investors wary.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed, investors wary.

text.p: U.S. shares trading in London were mixed to slightly firmer on Tuesday but volume was thin, with many European investors staying clear of the market due to its current high level and the dollar's strength, dealers said.
"The general market is steady around the New York close although a few stocks are a bit better," one dealer said.

"The strength of the dollar makes things more expensive and the high market level has discouraged some people," he said. "Europeans have generally been profit-takers over the last six months and are a bit loathed to get in at these higher levels."
March S&P 500 futures were up 1.00 at 796.25 by 1140 GMT.
Oil drilling shares were among the best performers in London. Baker Hughes Inc gained $1/4 to $35, Schlumberger Ltd rose $1/4 to $98-3/4 and Halliburton climbed $1/4 to $62.
Insurance group Aetna Life and Casualty Co was boosted by favourable press comment, gaining $3/8 to $85-1/8, dealers said.

U.S. January leading indicators, due at 1500 GMT, are the short term focus, dealers said. But most players are looking beyond this data to Wednesday's Humphrey Hawkins testimony by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan and Friday's February U.S. employment report, they said.
The Dow is expected to remain volatile. "The market is changing so quickly that daily predictions are a waste of time," one dealer said. "So are hourly predictions."
